lectures.title: Why are some countries rich and others poor?
What is it that is scarce?
Is economics a topic or a method?
Why use models that are obviously false?
Why do people trade at all?
Why is water cheap and diamonds expensive?
Where does a price come from if nobody sets it?
What happens when demand rises or supply falls?
Why did the price of oil quadruple in 1973?
How do we measure how rich a country is?
Is GDP the right measure of how well we live?
What do we know so far, and what don't we?
Do markets work — and what would that even mean?
How sensitive are buyers to price?
Who really pays a tax?
How much do buyers and sellers gain from a market?
What does a tax destroy?
What happens when the government caps rents?
What happens when the government sets a minimum price?
How does a price coordinate millions who never meet?
What happens when prices are not allowed to move?

quiz.question: Country A grows 1% a year, country B 3%. Both start at $2,000 a head. After 70 years, roughly how many times richer is B than A?
A poor country manages 7% growth a year. Roughly how many years until its income per person doubles?
A student could earn $20,000 a year in a job. Instead she studies, paying $8,000 a year in fees. What does a year of study cost her?
A surgeon earning $300 an hour and a student earning $15 an hour each queue two hours for free festival tickets. For whom is the free ticket dearer?
Which of these is economics?
choices: Bread and the tip: money changes hands

quiz.question: A city doubles its parking fine but halves its patrols, so a ticket is half as likely. In Becker's simplest model, what happens to illegal parking?
Day-care centres in Haifa started fining parents who came late. Late pickups rose, and stayed up after the fine was dropped. What fits best?
choices: The fine turned a duty into a price

quiz.question: A traffic model treats every driver as identical and perfectly informed, and has predicted rush-hour jams well for ten years. What would Friedman say?
choices: Keep using it: it predicts well

quiz.question: The city now brings in a congestion toll. Why might the same traffic model start to fail?
choices: Drivers change routes and times in ways it ignored

quiz.question: A model of Harbourtown's fishing grounds assumes every fisher catches the same amount. Which question does that assumption most endanger?
choices: How the fish price moves after a storm
Who in town gets richest from fishing
Whether a storm cuts the total catch

quiz.question: Mia is better at both jobs. Can trading with Jon still make her better off?
choices: No, he has nothing she needs

quiz.question: A surgeon types faster than her assistant. Who should type her letters?
In a day Ana makes 6 shirts or 3 tables; Ben makes 2 shirts or 2 tables. Who should make the tables?
choices: Ana: she is better at both

quiz.question: Making a car costs Freeland 3 tons of wheat, and Agraria 5 tons. At which price can both gain when Freeland sells cars for wheat?
Why does a diamond cost more than a glass of water?
choices: Diamonds take more work to dig out
It depends on how much of each we already have

quiz.question: Harbourtown's reservoir runs low and water is rationed. What happens to what people would pay for one more litre?
choices: It stays the same: water is just as useful

quiz.question: Labs learn to grow diamonds identical to mined ones, cheaply and in any number. What happens to the price of a diamond?
choices: It falls toward the cost of growing one
It stays high: diamonds are still beautiful
It rises: more people can now get one

quiz.question: Air is more useful than water or diamonds, yet it is free. Why?
choices: One more breath is worth nothing when air is everywhere
The government sets its price at zero

quiz.question: Crates are left over at $7. Which way will the price move?
Concert tickets sell out in minutes and are resold for three times the price. What does that tell you about the original price?
Where would you expect the price of the same old lamp to vary more from one sale to the next?
choices: A flea market where each buyer haggles alone
An auction room where everyone hears every bid

quiz.question: A storm keeps Harbourtown's fishing boats in port for a week. What happens to the price of fish and the amount sold?
A summer festival fills Harbourtown with mainland visitors. What happens at Mia's bakery?
Bread gets dearer, and Harbourtown families buy less bread. What is that, for the families?
choices: A move along their demand curve

quiz.question: A cheaper oven cuts Mia's costs just as a sourdough craze sweeps the town. What can we say for sure?
A cap holds the price below where supply and demand now meet. What happens?
A frost destroys 5% of the world's coffee crop. Drinkers barely change their habits for months, and new bushes take years to grow. The price will most likely…
Ten years after an oil cut, people have bought efficient cars and new oil fields have opened. An equal second cut would raise the price…
How much does this add to Harbourtown's GDP?
A carpenter buys wood for $300 and sells the table for $800. How much does the carpenter's work add to GDP?
Country X's income per person is $4,000 at market exchange rates, and its prices are about half America's. Roughly what is it at PPP?
A government wants to know how many foreign-made vaccines its economy could pay for. Which measure fits?
Norway puts most of its oil income into a fund instead of spending it. On Jones and Klenow's welfare measure, Norway looks…
choices: about as rich as its GDP

quiz.question: After a hurricane, a town spends a year rebuilding the houses it lost. What happens to its GDP that year?
Flour got dearer and a cheap rival opened, both in the same month. What can we say for sure about Mia's bread?
A new harbour crane lets the same crews land twice the fish. What happens on the picture?
choices: The town slides along the frontier
The town moves inside the frontier

quiz.question: Ola can make 4 nets or 2 oars in a day; Sara 1 net or 1 oar. Who should make the oars?
choices: Nobody gains from splitting the work

quiz.question: When economists say a market 'works', which test do they usually mean first?
Two economists agree that a congestion charge would cut city traffic by a fifth and hit poorer drivers hardest. One backs it, the other opposes it. What is the most likely reason?
choices: One of them has the facts wrong
They weigh efficiency and fairness differently
One of them doesn't understand markets

quiz.question: A city's taxi market is congested and overpriced. Is that enough to justify the city running the taxis itself?
choices: Yes: a failing market justifies stepping in
Not by itself: how well the city would run them must be compared too

quiz.question: Harbourtown's ferry raises its fares by 10%, and trips fall by 4%. What happens to the ferry's fare takings?
A city doubles its downtown parking fees. When is the drop in car trips biggest?
Smokers barely cut back when cigarettes cost more; tobacco firms can easily sell elsewhere. Who bears most of a cigarette tax?
Parliament moves the whole payroll tax from employers to workers' payslips. Once wages adjust, what does the simple model predict for take-home pay?
Wikipedia is free to read. What does its zero price tell us about what readers gain from it?
choices: Nothing: the gain is its worth above a zero price
Readers gain nothing, since they pay nothing
The gain equals the donations it receives

quiz.question: A concert sells out at $60 a ticket. Which buyer gains least?
choices: The fan who would have paid $200
The fan who would have paid just $60

quiz.question: The harbour council asks what a new ferry is worth to Harbourtown. Which number comes closest?
choices: Riders' value above the fare, plus the operator's margin over cost

quiz.question: Double the tax from $1 to $2. Roughly how many times bigger does the deadweight loss get?
A city doubles its hotel tax from $5 to $10 a night. Roughly what happens to the deadweight loss?
Which tax wastes least?
choices: A tax on one brand of cola

quiz.question: A country taxes imported bananas so heavily that nobody imports any. The tax raises nothing. What does it cost?
choices: The bananas people no longer get to eat
Exactly what it would have raised

quiz.question: Harbourtown's council caps the fee for a harbour mooring at half the market fee. What follows?
A city caps rents at $3,000 a month where the market rent is $2,000. What happens?
A hard rent cap stays in place for ten years. Compared with year one, the shortage is…
Which design protects sitting tenants while giving landlords the least reason to stop renting?
choices: Government pays part of a sitting tenant's large rent rise
A hard cap on every rent
The cap extended to new buildings

quiz.question: A country sets a minimum price for wheat below what wheat sells for anyway. What happens?
Before 1978, US regulators kept air fares high and airlines could not undercut them. What would you expect to see?
A minimum price for milk, and nobody buys up what is left over. Which farmers gain?
What does the cannery need to know before it uses less tin?
choices: Which of the two causes it was
Where the tin is needed most
Only that tin now costs more

quiz.question: Copper suddenly gets dearer, and an electrician switches some jobs to aluminium wire without knowing why. Which fits Hayek?
choices: She is doing the right thing without knowing the cause
She should wait until she knows the cause
Only a planner could tell her to switch

quiz.question: A factory dumps its waste into a river for free. What is wrong with the price of what it makes?
choices: It says the product is cheaper to make than it really is
Nothing: a price always carries the full cost

quiz.question: A concert sells tickets at $50, though fans would pay $300, and resale is banned. What decides who gets in?
choices: Nothing: fans just get a bargain

quiz.question: A city makes downtown parking free. Where does the gap go?
choices: Into time spent circling for a space

quiz.question: After a flood, every household gets a water coupon, and coupons may be sold. Compared with one long queue, what changes?
choices: Those who need less sell to those who need more, and no time is lost queuing
